title: Can You Pay to Appear in AI Answers? Ads Yes, Recommendations No
metaTitle: Can You Pay to Appear in AI Answers? Ads Yes, Answers No
metaDescription: You can buy ads in Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Copilot, but not the organic answer. A checked table of where ads run (Oct 2026) and how to earn a mention.
primaryKeyword: can you pay to appear in chatgpt
shortAnswer: You can pay for ads near or inside some AI answers, but not for the organic answer itself. As of October 2026, Google runs ads in AI Overviews and is testing them in AI Mode, OpenAI shows ads to some ChatGPT Free and Go users, and Microsoft sells Copilot ads. Each labels them as ads, and OpenAI says ads do not influence ChatGPT's answers. Earning a mention takes work, not budget.
intro:
The question mixes two products. An ad is a labelled slot that a platform sells you. A recommendation is the list of brands the model writes itself. Ads on AI surfaces are real and growing; recommendations are still not for sale.

This guide is based on each company's public pages, checked on 3 October 2026. We have not bought or run any of these ad products ourselves.

sections.heading: Can you pay to appear in AI answers?
sections.body:
Yes for ads, no for the answer. You can buy a labelled ad slot on several AI surfaces, but no engine sells a place in its own recommendation. Google says it [does not accept payment to rank pages higher](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works), and OpenAI says [advertisers cannot shape, rank or alter ChatGPT's responses](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt).

There are two different things people mean by "appearing in an AI answer":

- **An ad.** A slot the platform sells, labelled as an ad, priced by auction or bid, usually below the answer.
- **A recommendation.** The brand names the model writes itself after retrieving and weighing sources. It has no price.

One format blurs that line. Google's [20 May 2026 announcement](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/google-marketing-live-search-ads/) says ads can be "eligible to appear on that list" when AI Mode returns a list of recommendations, as a Highlighted Answer. Google calls it a test, says it stays labelled "Sponsored", and shows an independent AI explainer beside the ad.

Our reading: paying buys a labelled card inside the list, not a change to the list. Google does not say whether paying affects the organic list either way, and we cannot test it, so do not budget on the assumption that it does.

![Blue payment terminal with a receipt and gold coins on a blue background](https://images.pexels.com/photos/12920746/pexels-photo-12920746.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: Where do ads appear in AI search today?
sections.body:
Ads exist today in Google AI Overviews, in Google AI Mode (as a test), in ChatGPT for some Free and Go users, and in Microsoft Copilot. Perplexity has stepped back from ads and Claude is ad-free. This table reflects each company's own pages as checked on 3 October 2026; formats change quickly, so re-check before you plan spend.

| Surface | Ads? | Where they appear | What the source says |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google AI Overviews | Yes | Above, below or within the Overview | Text and Shopping ads; [within-Overview ads are English-only in 12 countries including the US](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/16297775?hl=en); not shown for sensitive verticals such as finance and healthcare |
| Google AI Mode | Testing | Below and integrated into the response | New formats announced [May 2026](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/google-marketing-live-search-ads/): Conversational Discovery ads and Highlighted Answers, labelled "Sponsored" |
| ChatGPT | Test, Free and Go plans | Below the end of a response | [Testing began in the US on 9 February 2026](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt); no ads for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Edu |
| Microsoft Copilot | Yes | Below the organic Copilot response | [Microsoft's July 2025 post describes an "Ad Voice" explaining why an ad is relevant](https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en/blog/post/july-2025/how-generative-ai-is-reshaping-search-a-qa-with-nicole-schumacher); [Offer Highlights added in April 2026](https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en/blog/post/april-2026/win-across-all-three-eras-of-the-web) |
| Perplexity | Not now | None | [Reported in February 2026](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/02/18/perplexity-abandons-ai-advertising/): sponsored answers phased out in 2025, no plan to return |
| Claude | No | None | Anthropic: ["Claude will remain ad-free"](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-is-a-space-to-think) (4 February 2026) |

The Google Ads Help page for AI Overviews contains the detail that matters most to buyers. You [cannot opt out, cannot target placements inside AI Overviews directly, and get no segmented reporting](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/16297775?hl=en) for them. So you cannot see what share of your spend ran there, which makes ad spend a poor way to measure AI visibility.

We did not verify whether ads run in the Gemini app, so it is not in the table.

sections.heading: Can you pay for organic AI recommendations?
sections.body:
No. No engine sells organic recommendations, and the ones that comment say so. Google states it [does not accept payment to rank pages higher](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works). OpenAI says [ChatGPT's product results are selected independently, are not ads, and are not influenced by partnerships](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search).

People still pay for three things that sit next to the answer. Here is our view of each:

1. **Sponsored posts on other sites.** Do not expect these to earn citations. In a University of Toronto study of a web-enabled GPT, US software queries drew [72.7% earned media and 26.7% brand-owned sources](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08919), against 45.4% and 43.7% for Google. We have no data on whether engines discount sponsored posts, and Google's [spam policies](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) treat paid articles with ranking-credit links as link spam.
2. **Agencies and tools.** You pay for work or measurement, never for placement. A guarantee that you will be named is a red flag; our [nine questions to ask an AEO agency](/blog/answer-engine-optimization-agency) cover what to ask instead.
3. **Product feeds.** This is data, not a purchase. OpenAI's help page says Shopify merchants are already integrated through Shopify Catalog and that other merchants [can apply for direct product-feed access](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search). Complete, current product data is the closest thing to a lever e-commerce brands have.

![A cardboard hand holding a coin above a jar, standing for saving instead of spending](https://images.pexels.com/photos/5849596/pexels-photo-5849596.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: Should you buy ads on AI surfaces anyway?
sections.body:
Buy AI-surface ads only when the query is commercial and your ad already converts in classic search, and budget them separately from AI visibility. An ad stops when the budget does. A recommendation earned from independent coverage does not depend on your spend, and it is the more valuable of the two.

Why we say recommendations are worth more, with a caveat. In AEOeye's recommendation benchmark (127 audits from 26 June to 7 September 2026, 27 brand names), 71.4% of 147 ranked brand mentions were in first place. That sample is small and self-selected, so treat it as a pattern, not a market rate; the [measurement hub](/blog/ai-brand-recommendation-measurement) lists the numbers and limits, and the [benchmark file](/resources/aeoeye-recommendation-benchmark-2026-09.json) is public. The pattern: when an answer names your brand, it usually names it first.

Practical limits to know before you spend:

- **Google** requires [AI-powered targeting such as broad match, AI Max, Performance Max, Shopping campaigns or Dynamic Search Ads](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/16297775?hl=en) for ads in AI Overviews.
- **OpenAI** says ad ranking considers [relevance and advertiser bids](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt), and ads are not eligible near sensitive topics such as personal health, mental health or politics.
- **Both** keep ads visibly separate, so a good ad does not make the model say your name in its own text.

sections.heading: How do you earn AI recommendations instead?
sections.body:
Measure where you stand, keep AI crawlers allowed, earn independent coverage, and make your pages easy to quote. This takes weeks, not a budget line, but it is the only route that changes what the engine writes. [How AI assistants decide which brands to recommend](/blog/how-ai-assistants-choose-brands) explains the mechanics.

1. **Measure first.** Ask each engine ten buyer questions without naming your brand, then repeat on another day, because answers vary. AEOeye's [free audit](/) runs three unbranded questions live on ChatGPT and shows the real answers. Engines differ, so check each one separately.
2. **Do not block retrieval bots.** OpenAI says [sites opted out of OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots). In AEOeye's crawler access study (October 2026, 384 sites), only 1 of 193 SaaS sites blocked any AI retrieval bot, so for most brands the gap lies elsewhere. The [crawler directory](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory) has the data.
3. **Earn third-party coverage.** Reviews, comparisons and roundups written by others were the sources AI search leaned on in the Toronto test above, so that is where to earn mentions.
4. **State who you are, consistently, and write quotable pages.** Use the same brand name, category and who-it-is-for line on your site, directories and profiles so an engine can identify you. Google says [no special optimization is needed for AI Overviews or AI Mode](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features); a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet. There is no setting to buy either. See [what an AI Overview is](/blog/what-is-an-ai-overview).
5. **Re-measure in batches** and fix the largest gap first, following [how to get your business recommended by AI](/blog/how-to-get-your-business-recommended-by-ai).

![A green plant growing from a jar of coins on a table](https://images.pexels.com/photos/6774947/pexels-photo-6774947.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

keyTakeaways: Ads in AI surfaces are real (Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT Free and Go tests, Copilot); organic recommendations are not for sale.
Google's AI Mode test lets ads appear as a labelled Highlighted Answer in a recommendation list, but it remains an ad.
You cannot opt out of, target, or separately report on Google ads inside AI Overviews, so ad spend does not measure AI visibility.
Perplexity has reportedly stepped back from ads, and Anthropic says Claude will remain ad-free.
The route that changes the answer is slower: allow AI crawlers, earn independent coverage, publish quotable pages.

faqs.a: Yes, in a test. OpenAI's help center says ads may appear for users on the Free and Go plans, below the end of a response, labelled as sponsored and visually separated. Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu accounts do not see ads. OpenAI says ads do not influence ChatGPT's answers, and advertisers can sign up at ads.openai.com.

faqs.q: Can I pay Google to appear in AI Overviews?
faqs.a: You can pay for ads that Google may show above, below or within AI Overviews, but not for the Overview's own text. Google Ads Help says ads appear when its systems find commercial intent and a relevant ad, require AI-powered targeting such as broad match, and cannot be opted out of or targeted to AI Overviews alone.

faqs.q: Does Perplexity or Claude sell ads?
faqs.a: Not currently, according to the sources we checked. Anthropic states that Claude will remain ad-free and that responses will not be influenced by advertisers. Perplexity phased out sponsored answers in 2025, and executives told the Financial Times in February 2026 that they do not plan to revisit them, as reported by MacRumors.

faqs.q: Do ads change which brands an AI recommends?
faqs.a: OpenAI says no: ads run on separate systems from its chat model, and advertisers cannot shape or rank responses. Google describes AI Mode ads as separately labelled units but does not say whether they affect organic lists. We have not tested either claim, so measure your own answers before and after any campaign.

faqs.q: How do I get recommended by AI without paying?
faqs.a: Check which buyer questions name you, keep AI search crawlers allowed in robots.txt, earn independent reviews and comparisons, and publish pages that state facts clearly enough to quote. Then re-check in batches, because answers vary from run to run. Expect weeks rather than days.
